history: Clean at v1.4.1907 (correct add i32 %1, -1); regressed at v1.5.2010; reproduces at every stable release from v1.5.2010 through v1.9.2607 with no reversion (linear scan, 20 probeable releases) and on main-debug. One clean transition, not oscillating -- the tool's 'non-monotonic' label here just reflects run-count, see method-notes.md.

summary: Reproduces on main (89e2f98e2, Debug). Func(--i) -- an empty inout function called with a pre-decremented argument -- lowers the single decrement to 'add i32 %N, -2' instead of -1; controls confirm neither a bare inout call nor a bare pre-decrement alone triggers it, only the combination written directly as the argument expression. Regressed between v1.4.1907 (clean) and v1.5.2010; reproduces at every release since and on main-debug. The maintainer's cited fix vehicle (tracking issue #5377) was closed not_planned 2024-09-16 and the draft PR it points to (#5249) is still open/unmerged, so that rewrite never reached main -- consistent with the still-reproducing probes. Separately, Compiler Explorer's hlsl_clang_trunk (the new Clang-based HLSL front end) already emits the correct 'add i32 ..., -1' for the identical construct, while classic dxc_trunk still emits -2.
text_stale: 2023-07-08 maintainer comment says the fix is verified against a development branch and will land via #5377; that tracking issue was closed not_planned on 2024-09-16 and the linked draft PR #5249 is still open/unmerged, so the branch never reached main and the comment now reads as resolved when it is not.
title: When using "--variable" as an argument to an inout function, 2 is subtracted not one
